subject: Transfer mechanism options and subprocessor proof request
messages:
From: Jonathan Meyer <jonathan.meyer@medibridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@novacare-legal.co.uk>
Date: 2027-08-24T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Transfer safeguards + subprocessor proof for EU/UK rollout

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — MediBridge is targeting a staged rollout across Germany and the UK in Q4, and our legal team has surfaced a few items we need to close before going live. High level asks:

- Confirmation of the primary transfer mechanism(s) you propose for EU -> non-EEA processing and UK processing (SCCs, UK IDTA/UK Addendum, TIA/DTIA).
- A sample signed attestation or template for subprocessor controls we can attach to our DPA.
- A current subprocessor matrix (names, roles, data categories, regions).
- Evidence that logs/telemetry with user-generated data are retained in the EU (or otherwise segregated) and the retention schedule.

We appreciate that Redwood supports multiple deployment options; for MediBridge we prefer to stay on the hosted API if possible, but will consider Dedicated if it materially reduces legal friction. Can you outline both the legal pathway (which transfer mechanism + docs) and the operational evidence we should provide to our privacy team?

Would you be able to share a draft attestation and the subprocessor spreadsheet today? Our counsel (Sarah Ellis) is on copy.

Thanks,
Jonathan Meyer
Head of IT Operations
MediBridge GmbH

Attachment: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Meyer <jonathan.meyer@medibridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer safeguards + subprocessor proof for EU/UK rollout

Thanks Jonathan — great question and totally reasonable for a regulated rollout. Quick summary up front, followed by next steps and attachments.

Summary (short):
- Primary path: SCCs (EU) + UK Addendum (IDTA) where required.
- Supplement: TIA/DTIA scoping used to document technical and organizational safeguards (exposure matrix, retention, crypto).
- Fallback/option: Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment for customers who want physical/tenant isolation and to minimize subprocessor surface.

What we'll share now (attached):
- "RBW_subprocessor_matrix_2027.xlsx" — current list of subprocessors with roles and processing locations.
- "subprocessor_attestation_template.docx" — template attestation / controls checklist you can attach to the DPA.

Operational notes:
- Hosted API path: We offer SCCs executed via the DPA + UK Addendum for UK-resident data flows. For higher-assurance use cases we provide a TIA/DTIA workbook that maps the product features (KV caches, prefix caching, telemetry) to the safeguards. That workbook is what your privacy team will want to see.
- Logs: Production request logs (traces, token counts) are stored in-region for EU customers by default and retained per customer retention config; we can provide a sample retention export and canonical locations. Full request payloads are not retained beyond the default retention period unless explicitly enabled for debugging by the customer.
- Encryption & keys: Data at rest is encrypted using KMS (customer-tenant or Redwood-managed). If you require a customer-managed key we can add that under Dedicated/Private options.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Laura (copied) will send a short attestation template pre-filled with Redwood defaults and an explanation of any fields that usually require customer input.
2) Kimberly — can you confirm the default EU log retention window and provide an export sample?
3) Jonathan/Sarah — review the attached matrix & attestation and let us know if you need a signed copy or additional evidence (SOC2 artifact excerpts, network topology diagram, or a copy of our TIA workbook).

We can also set up a 30-minute call with Laura and our infra lead if your team prefers to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RBW_subprocessor_matrix_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet), subprocessor_attestation_template.docx (docx)
From: Jonathan Meyer <jonathan.meyer@medibridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@novacare-legal.co.uk>
Date: 2027-08-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer safeguards + subprocessor proof for EU/UK rollout

Thanks Sergio — received the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions from our privacy team:

1) Can Redwood scope the SCCs/TIA such that certain subprocessors (analytics vendor) are excluded from processing EU personal data for MediBridge? We need to know whether we can contractually block a subprocessor at the account level or whether that requires switching to Dedicated/Private.
2) The attestation template is helpful — would you provide a sample *signed* attestation or is that only for enterprise/Dedicated customers?
3) For UK specifically, will Redwood execute the UK IDTA/UK Addendum or do you rely on the EU SCCs + a separate MLA?
4) For logs: please confirm the default retention window (days) and whether logs that contain pseudonymized tokens ever leave EU data centers. Sarah has flagged an item on capture of IPs in telemetry.

If you can answer these in writing we'll pass to our legal team; if not, a quick call with Laura and your infra/security lead works too.

—Jonathan
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Meyer <jonathan.meyer@medibridge.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer safeguards + subprocessor proof for EU/UK rollout

Jonathan / Sarah — Laura from Redwood legal here. Quick answers to each of your questions, and I've attached a pre-signed attestation example for your review (note: the signed example is a redacted template we provide to mid-market customers; final signed attestations are executed together with the DPA for enterprise customers on an SOW).

1) Subprocessor scoping:
- Hosted API: We cannot selectively disable a Redwood-managed subprocessor at the account level (e.g., turning off our analytics vendor for one tenant) because many of our shared services are multi-tenant. However, we can: 1) commit to contractual controls and data minimization for that subprocessor, and 2) provide a plan to route sensitive EU workloads to Dedicated/Private where a subset of subprocessors are not used.

2) Signed attestation:
- Attached "subprocessor_attestation_signed_sample.pdf" — this is a standard, redacted example. For enterprise engagements we execute a signed attestation tied to the DPA and provide notarized sign-off on request.

3) UK mechanism:
- We will execute the UK Addendum (IDTA) in conjunction with the EU SCCs when required by UK-resident data processing. Our standard approach for customers with both EU and UK footprints is: SCCs + UK Addendum + TIA workbook that maps safeguards. That is the fastest legal route for hosted customers.

4) Logs/telemetry:
- Default retention window: 30 days for request-level logs (configurable by the customer up to 180 days).
- Telemetry IP capture: we pseudonymize IPs in telemetry by default; raw IPs are only retained for a short troubleshooting window and are stored in-region for EU customers. They are not exported outside the EU unless required for security incident response and with appropriate legal process.

Attachments included: RBW_subprocessor_matrix_2027.xlsx (as shared earlier), subprocessor_attestation_template.docx (template), subprocessor_attestation_signed_sample.pdf (redacted signed sample)

If you'd like, we can prepare a concise package (DPA with SCCs/UK Addendum + signed attestation + TIA workbook excerpts + subprocessor matrix) for your procurement/legal review. Happy to get that to you by EOD tomorrow if that timeline helps.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
